title: Getting our long videos seen
goal: Long videos to thousands of views each.
why: All 16 long videos together were shown about 4,050 times in three and a half months.
About 2% of the people who saw one clicked it.
Viewers watched 15% to 25% of a film on average.
The Shorts feed hands every Short its viewers. A long gets no such start on a channel with 19 subscribers.

steps.name: Journey film (58 minutes)
steps.what: A calm documentary from Earth to the dying star Betelgeuse, made from seven finished films.

steps.name: Sleep film (1 hour 48 minutes)
steps.what: A slow space documentary to fall asleep to, from the Moon to Andromeda, titled and tagged from research on channels that do this.

steps.name: Every planet explained in 10 minutes

title: Orbit from January: films people search for
goal: Long videos found through search by adults in English-speaking countries, building to thousands of views each.
why: Our topics came from subjects big channels already own, and YouTube rarely shows a 19-subscriber channel beside them.
Space searches with real demand and weak results exist: 'space mysteries' 134,000 a month (competition 43), 'milky way' 96,000 (38), 'documentary for sleep' 123,000 (44).
Orbit's Shorts get 100 to 1,300 views each, so they keep running and test topics before a long is made.

steps.name: First weekly search research
steps.what: The searches, countries, results-page gaps and small-channel breakouts for about 50 space subjects, ranked into clusters. Then every Monday.

steps.what: Keep two a week if search views are growing; if not, options to Ben.

The first January long uses the July illustrated style with the Orbit mascot, as a style test.
Run two search-led longs a week from January (Wednesday and Sunday at 18:00 London) plus four Shorts a week.

title: Starting our WW2 documentary channel
goal: Monetised as fast as possible, then a lot of views: three films a week (Tue, Thu, Sat 17:00 London) from Sat 28 Nov 2026, about 25 minutes now (<=21,000 chars) and 35-45 minutes after the voice upgrade, aiming at 1,000 subscribers and 4,000 watch hours before YouTube's bar for new channels doubles to 8,000 hours on 1 Feb 2027.
why: Why this niche (vidIQ, checked against the YouTube API, 17 Nov): WW2 Dossier, started 30 Apr 2026, passed 1,000 subscribers 13 days after its first upload and has 14,300, on 39-56 minute archive-photo films with no Shorts. 'world war 2' gets 564,442 searches a month and 'ww2 documentary' 261,896.
Its own rules (channels/ww2/studio/RULES.md) and playbook (00_Brand/PLAYBOOK.md), written fresh: Ben is asked only to watch finished films; the Chief locks topics after review.
Name: Field Order History is the recommendation (its handle was free on 17 Nov). Ben picks when he creates the channel.
Voice: at most 21,000 ElevenLabs characters a film, and two pilot films voiced, until Ben upgrades the plan.
Its own repo, TheLaughingGod1986/ww2-channel (made 17 Nov): the channel moves there with its history (J3009), and the board shows it before launch (J3007).

steps.name: Channel set-up: own repo, on the board, channel kit
steps.what: Move into TheLaughingGod1986/ww2-channel with its history, show the channel on the board before launch (films, review, Ben's ticks), and the profile picture, banner, description and upload template ready for Ben.

steps.name: Packaging library and the channel's own numbers
steps.what: Which WW2 titles and thumbnails beat their channel's usual views (YouTube API, monthly), and from the first upload the 48-hour and 7-day reads and a card for 1,000 subscribers and 4,000/8,000 watch hours.

steps.name: Pilot 1: How Britain Built Two Harbours in Secret and Floated Them to Normandy
steps.what: Mulberry A & B artificial harbours (65 chars): 212 6,000-ton concrete caissons, floating Whale roadways, the June 1944 gale and PLUTO. IWM + US NARA photos & code maps; 4.88M / 1.94M / 973K neighbours; thumb 'BUILT IN 12 DAYS'; 25 min (~20,000 voice chars, Slot 1 of 2).

steps.name: Pilot 2: How the Allies Closed the U-Boats' Safest Hunting Ground
steps.what: Closing the Mid-Atlantic air gap in 'Black May' 1943 (64 chars): VLR B-24 Liberators, escort carriers, 10 cm radar and HF/DF sinking 43 U-boats in one month. IWM Coastal Command + US Navy photos & range-ring maps; 4.13M / 1.59M / 1.30M neighbours; 25 min (~20,000 voice chars, Slot 2 of 2).

steps.name: Pilot 3: Why America's Most Expensive WW2 Weapon Wasn't the Atomic Bomb
steps.what: America's $3.0B bomber gamble vs the $1.9B Manhattan Project (65 chars): pressurised crew tunnels, GE analog gun computers, magnesium R-3350 fires, the snowy 'Battle of Kansas' and Tokyo's 200-mph jet stream. USAAF NARA + LoC colour archive; 4.02M / 1.96M / 1.20M neighbours; thumb '$3 BILLION GAMBLE'; 26 min (~20,800 chars — script & harvest £0 now, voice after ElevenLabs upgrade/renewal).

steps.name: Film 4: Why America's Submarine Torpedoes Failed for 21 Months in WW2
steps.what: The Mark 14 torpedo scandal in the Pacific, Dec 1941 to Sep 1943 (61 chars): running 10 feet too deep, faulty magnetic exploders, crushed contact pins, and unauthorized live tests at Maui and Fremantle. US NHHC + NARA submarine archive; 1.67M / 1.43M / 1.32M neighbours.

steps.name: Film 5: How an Old Destroyer Became a Bomb to Keep Tirpitz Out of the Atlantic
steps.what: Operation Chariot at St Nazaire, March 1942 (61 chars): disguising the 1919 destroyer HMS Campbeltown with 4.25 tons of delayed-fuse explosives to deny Tirpitz the Normandie dry dock. UK IWM Admiralty + TNA files; 8.19M / 4.57M / 1.30M neighbours.

steps.name: Film 6: Why Britain Built Its Fastest WW2 Bomber Out of Plywood and Balsa
steps.what: The de Havilland DH.98 Mosquito (65 chars): unarmed birch-and-balsa fuselages moulded in furniture workshops, carrying a 4,000-lb Cookie bomb to Berlin at 400 mph with a 0.7% loss rate. UK IWM Air Ministry + TNA archive; 5.39M / 3.11M / 2.39M neighbours.

steps.name: Film 7: How Floating Dry Docks Kept Damaged US Fleets Fighting Off Japan
steps.what: Service Squadron 10 and Ulithi Atoll (64 chars): towing sectional floating dry docks able to lift 90,000 tons 5,000 miles west of Pearl Harbor alongside 617 anchored ships. US NHHC + NARA RG 80-G archive; 3.69M / 3.25M / 2.41M neighbours.

steps.name: Film 8: How One Planted Briefcase Pulled German Divisions Away From Sicily
steps.what: Operation Mincemeat, spring 1943 (66 chars): building a complete paper life for fictitious 'Major William Martin', drifting fake invasion plans ashore from submarine HMS Seraph, and tracking Hitler's divisions via Ultra. UK TNA CAB 154 / WO 208 + IWM archive; 3.14M / 2.03M / 1.43M neighbours.

steps.name: Film 9: How One Wrecked Oil Tanker Saved Starving Malta in August 1942
steps.what: Operation Pedestal and the tanker SS Ohio (62 chars): torpedoed, bombed and broken-backed, yet brought into Valletta's Grand Harbour with 11,500 tons of fuel lashed between two Royal Navy destroyers. UK IWM Admiralty + US Merchant Marine archive; 683K / 570K / 312K neighbours.

steps.name: Film 10: Why Britain Built Flame, Flail and Bridge Tanks After Dieppe Failed
steps.what: 79th Armoured Division's specialist assault armour (67 chars): turning the 1942 Dieppe beach disaster into Sherman Crab mine-flails, AVRE petard bunker-busters, fascines, bridges and DD swimming tanks on D-Day. UK IWM War Office + TNA WO 205 archive; 3.33M / 1.23M / 701K neighbours.

steps.name: Film 11: How a British Engine Made the P-51 Mustang
steps.what: Pairing North American Aviation's airframe with the Rolls-Royce Merlin to solve the 1943 bomber-escort range crisis. US NARA RG 342-FH + LoC FSA/OWI + UK IWM; 2.89M / 1.45M neighbours.

steps.name: Film 12: How America Built a Liberty Ship in Four Days
steps.what: Welded pre-fabrication yards building Liberty ships at speed, and the brittle-steel cracking crisis. US NARA RG 178 + LoC FSA/OWI; 4.07M neighbour.

steps.name: Film 13: How the WW2 Ghost Army Fooled German Generals
steps.what: The 23rd Headquarters Special Troops' inflatable tanks, sound trucks and fake radio traffic. US NARA RG 111-SC + UK IWM; 319K / 131K neighbours.

steps.name: Film 14: How the Dambusters Bouncing Bomb Worked
steps.what: Barnes Wallis's spinning bouncing bomb and 617 Squadron's low-level run on the Ruhr dams (Christmas Eve slot: Ben's call on skipping). UK IWM Air Ministry; 2.03M / 1.83M neighbours.

steps.name: Film 15: Sherman Tank: How America Kept It Fighting
steps.what: How the M4 Sherman's shipping limits, field repair and numbers outlasted heavier German tanks (Boxing Day slot). US NARA RG 111-SC + LoC + UK IWM; 1.15M / 938K / 863K neighbours.

steps.name: Film 16: Battle of the Bulge, told through one narrow question
steps.what: Bletchley got an archive NO-GO (J3541). From the 24 Nov search research: 'battle of the bulge' 135,980 searches a month, 'battle of the bulge documentary' 8,206 at competition 38; one engineering or logistics question (Patton's 48-hour turn north, or the proximity fuze's first use on land), airing in the anniversary. US NARA RG 111 Signal Corps.

steps.name: Film 17: How the US Raised Pearl Harbor's Sunk Battleships
steps.what: From the 24 Nov search research: 'pearl harbor' 267,002 searches a month, 'pearl harbor documentary' 17,726 at competition 44, results-page gap 6 of 10; a 1,410-subscriber channel got 521,874 views on this story in Oct 2026. NHHC post-attack salvage photos + NARA RG 80-G.

decisions.text: Start a WW2 documentary channel: long films only, made with our ElevenLabs plan until the upgrade.
Ask me only to watch finished films; the studio decides everything else.
Its own rules and its own ideas, not Orbit's or History of Science's.
Its own GitHub repo, fully decoupled.
Bring both pilots forward to start testing earlier: pilot 1 on Sun 22 Nov at 17:00, pilot 2 on Wed 25 Nov at 17:00 (three days apart for a clean 48-hour read on pilot 1).
Move pilot 2 (J9WGu8aPnHI) from Wed 25 Nov 17:00 to Sat 28 Nov 17:00 London (17:00Z) to fit the approved new opening on top of the archive upgrade (J3364). Films 003-006 dates unchanged.

Three films a week (Tue, Thu, Sat 17:00 London). Pilot 2 airs Tue 24 Nov, then Sat 28 Nov, Tue 1 Dec, Thu 3 Dec, Sat 5 Dec and so on (in chat ~09:55: "we're not missing Saturday 28th"). Ben's watch three days before air; a film that isn't ready skips its slot.

title: History of Science from January: films English-speaking adults search for
goal: Long videos found through search by adults in the US, UK, Canada and Australia, building to thousands of views each.
why: Full HOS audit (J3223, 20 Nov): all 7 longs together got 2,185 showings and 233 settled views (best long 162 on Periodic Table; the other 6 averaged 12 views).

Audience is already adult (78.8% aged 25-54, 70.2% male), but reported Anglosphere views are 86% UK (811) with US at only 2.5% (109 lifetime; below threshold in the last 28 days) while school-cram traffic in India and SE Asia outnumbers US+CA+AU by 3.3x.
Story-first titles and health/vaccine topics failed reach, while US Education long-form pays about $3.42 mid RPM ($2.05-$5.47, vidIQ).

vidIQ + signed-out US top-10 research (J3224) found 4 clusters with 7/10-10/10 results-page gaps and sub-50k US breakouts (5x-77x): Electricity & Rivalries, Nuclear & Modern Physics, Accidental Inventions, and Breakthrough & Lost Engineering.

steps.name: Film 1: Thomas Edison vs Nikola Tesla: How AC Won the War of Currents

Same 14-day bar (500 keep / 162 drop). Folder and topic review by 26 Nov, script draft 2 Dec, lock 11 Dec (J3495).

steps.name: Weekly cadence: 1 search-led long + 4 Shorts a week
steps.what: Long every Thursday 18:00 London (7-9 min, normal publish). Four 16-19 s 3D cartoon question Shorts a week at 11:30 London (Fri, Sat, Sun, Tue): Sat & Fri promote the week's long; Sun & Tue rotate cluster winners or test next month's candidate topics before scripting.

steps.name: Our own search terms and Anglosphere read
steps.what: Monthly YouTube Analytics read of HOS search terms and US+UK+CA+AU share; double down on growing adult Anglosphere clusters and drop any cluster after ~3 films below the 162-view bar.

steps.name: Six-week review
steps.what: Read 14-day views, impressions, CTR and US+UK+CA+AU share across the four December search-led longs (10-31 Dec, the last 14-day read ends 14 Jan) and any January one with a full read. Keep winning clusters, cut weak ones, and decide whether to raise cadence or test one 45-60 min calm science-history compilation (after Orbit's Dec tests).

decisions.text: Full HOS audit completed: 4,352 settled views (94.5% Shorts, 5.4% longs), best long 162 views, 78.8% aged 25-54, US only 2.5% of lifetime views.
Search-led research and proposed 2027 HOS plan added to the board waiting for Ben's OK (LEARNINGS rule 34 item 7). Nothing changes on HOS until Ben says yes.

OK to the 2027 History of Science search-led plan: the four Anglosphere adult clusters, 1 search-led long (Thu 18:00) + 4 Shorts a week, the first four January films and the 14-day test bar (500+ keep, 162-499 one more, under 162 drop or change). "Please go ahead and start it." Films 008-011 and 013 stay untouched through December.

"That plan is HOS test that could turn around ... definitely worth a look this week. If we can get that one queued up and working straight away." All four January films start this week: HOS:128 entered production on 24 Nov (HOS places 4 to 5); films 2-4 topic reviews by 26 Nov and script drafts 28 Nov-2 Dec. Air dates stay 7, 14, 21 and 28 Jan.

"If we can move it from December to this Thursday, sounds like a good idea. I'll let you do your best call." Claude's call: Edison vs Tesla has no script yet, so it can't be made well by Thursday. 008 Franklin (finished, Chief PASS) takes Thu 26 Nov and 009 Gravity Thu 3 Dec, each after Ben's watch (J3500, J3501). The four search-led films move into December: 10, 17, 24 and 31 Dec. One that isn't ready slides a week and a finished older film (010, 011, 013) takes the Thursday. Six-week review moves to 21 Jan.

title: Grow what works: a monthly scorecard for every channel
goal: Put the studio's effort where it grows subscribers and watch hours: each channel is kept, grown or faded on its own numbers, month by month.
why: Last 30 days (24 Nov): Orbit With Ben 5 longs (typical 14 views) and 22 Shorts (typical 470), +3 subscribers, 8.6 long watch hours; History of Science 3 longs (typical 7) and 17 Shorts (typical 89), +3 subscribers, 4.1 hours; Field Order History 1 long (about 20 views on its first day), +1 subscriber.
Shorts bring views but few subscribers (Orbit about 0.3 per 1,000 Shorts views, History of Science about 1.3), and their watch time does not count towards the 4,000 hours.

Ben, 24 Nov: "monitor the channels, and channels that are not doing too good, slowly begin to fade them out for the channels that are doing good"; later: "I like your idea about fading out weak channels ... let's put that plan into action", with Orbit's and History of Science's coming tests given their chance first.

decisions.text: Schedules stay: Orbit With Ben 2 long + 4 Shorts a week, History of Science 1 long + 4 Shorts, Field Order History 3 long (Tue, Thu, Sat) from 1 Dec. A monthly scorecard decides; the weakest channel fades, but never while its own tests are running.

steps.name: Monthly channel scorecard on the board
steps.what: Per channel, last month against the month before: new subscribers, long-film watch hours, Shorts views, subscribers per 1,000 views, films made, and return per film made.

steps.name: First monthly review, after the December push
steps.what: Verdicts for Ben, nothing changes without his yes. Shorts keep their number while the typical Short's views rise and the channel gets at least 1 new subscriber per 1,000 Shorts views; otherwise 4 a week becomes 2 or 3. The channel lowest on return per film is recommended to halve its schedule for a month, giving that effort to the top channel; last again the month after, it stops new films (nothing is deleted). Orbit With Ben and History of Science are not cut while their tests run (Orbit's December long-film tests read to 30 Dec, its search-led six-week review is 14 Feb; History of Science's search-led review is 18 Feb); their numbers are still shown.
